newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Bimantara lays down long-term plans.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Bimantara lays down long-term plans.

text.p: Indonesian conglomerate PT Bimantara Citra, run by President Suharto's son Bambang Trihatmodjo, unveiled long-term strategies on Tuesday to strengthen revenues well into the next century.
Bimantara presented the plan at an analysts' meeting, saying the company's infrastructure division would contribute major long-term earnings in future.
"We have set up strategies to conduct our businesses from the short term to the long term and focus on seven core businesses," Kadir Assegaf, a director of Bimantara, told analysts.

"In the long run, the infrastructure sector is designed to lead the growth of the company," Assegaf said, adding that main core future income was expected from the company's gas pipeline off eastern Java, which is the longest gas pipeline in Asia.
PT Trans Javagas Pipeline is the fourth largest such pipeline in the world, stretching 430 km (267 miles) under the sea from the east Java island of Pagerungan Besar to Gresik in east Java.
The pipeline carries 300 million cubic feet of gas per day but is still functioning only at 50 percent of designed capacity.
Bimantara did not say when throughput would be expanded but said the firm began receiving a fee for gas transported in 1994, with payment continuing for 20 years.
It said revenues would go towards repaying bank loans, and by the year 2002 this source would yield the company a fixed net annual income of $46 million.
"This firm is predicted to play a main role among others in contribution for Bimantara after the year 2001," Assegaf said.

He said in the short term television station PT Rajawali Citra Televisi Indonesia (RCTI) would continue to play a major role in generating profits, followed by the transportation, automotive and telecommunication sectors.
"The growth rate of RCTI is expected to rise dramatically due to the consistent growth rate in television advertising expenditures," Assegaf said.
He added, however, that in the medium term the telecommunications sector was targeted to grow more rapidly than others.
Bimantara's telecommunications sector includes two units overseeing cellular communications, satellite operations, international telephone services and equipment manufacturing.
"In the medium term we are optimistic telecommunications will become a main contributor," Assegaf said.

Assegaf said that in the long term the infrastructure division would contribute the most revenue, followed by telecommunications, transportation and automobiles and media and broadcasting. "With this future plan we are confident Bimantara will continue to achieve outstanding performances," Assegaf said.

Analysts reacted positively, saying the conglomerate had transformed itself into a slick and professionally-run company from what had previously been dubbed as a conglomerate excessively dependent on political goodwill.
Trihatmodjo, Suharto's son and president-director of the conglomerate, was present at the meeting but did not speak.
"It's a well-managed company," said one analyst, adding that Bimantara had gone far beyond relying on government contracts for business.
Bimantara posted net profit growth of 33.7 percent to 157.5 billion rupiah ($66 million) last year.
